daef3612: Before arrival, guests need to know six things: the exact address, how to get there, where to park, how to get in, the Wi-Fi and who to call.
64d89b92: Send the instructions 1–2 days before arrival, and a short reminder on the day.

41a446e4: A guest arriving in an unfamiliar city for the first time, often tired and with luggage, doesn't need a novel. They need answers to the questions they would otherwise ask you by phone:
1e1eecc6: Exact address and a pin on the map. Street and number aren't always enough. In many parts of Sarajevo and other cities, navigation leads to the wrong entrance.
a87e0b00: Exact address and a pin on the map.
7ed498cb: How to get there. From the airport, bus or train station: taxi, bus, approximate travel time.
5428cb68: Parking. Whether the apartment has parking, where it is, whether it's paid and how. If not, where the nearest public garage is.
cbcb2d74: Entrance and keys. Which building, which entrance, floor, apartment number. Whether you meet them or it's self check-in.
18effd23: Wi-Fi. Network name and password. This is question number one after walking in.
ee289be2: Contact. The phone number and channel (WhatsApp, Viber) you answer on.
fe2ff707: You can send the house rules in the same message or as a separate link. There's a ready-made one in our house rules template.
b0d10758: Too early and guests forget them. Too late and they're already on their way without the information. The schedule that has worked best:
5ff4903c: Right after bookingA short thank-you and confirmation. Ask for the approximate arrival time.
48ad1e8e: 1–2 days before arrivalComplete instructions: address, getting there, parking, entrance, Wi-Fi, contact, house rules.
ca9d546a: On the day of arrivalA short reminder: “See you today, here's the link with the instructions.”
31506be2: The first morning of the stay“Is everything all right?” A small problem solved immediately doesn't end up in a review.

054d3233: 1. A photo is worth more than a description
0311157a: A photo of the building entrance, the apartment door and the key box solves most problems before they happen. A guest in the dark, facing three similar entrances, won't read a description — they'll look for the door from the picture.
028d397c: 2. Write from the guest's point of view
9db8994b: The apartment is in the building by the bakery.
746ff5fd: When you get out of the taxi you'll see a bakery. The building entrance is the green door to the right of it.
d1bc686c: When the information is scattered across five messages in the Airbnb chat, guests can't find the Wi-Fi password when they need it. Send everything in one message or, better still, as a single link guests can open at any time.
6b4e83b2: A guest from Germany or Turkey understands English, but reads instructions in their own language faster and with fewer mistakes, especially when tired after the journey.
3f317228: All the instructions in one link
e6176774: The SmartStay digital guide brings the address, parking, entrance, Wi-Fi, house rules and recommendations together in one link or QR code. Guests open it on their phone, automatically in their language, and the AI assistant answers questions while you sleep.
f29fffb7: Is it better to send the instructions as a message or a PDF?
4069ae75: A message or a link beats a PDF. PDFs are awkward to open on a phone, hard to search, and guests have to dig them out of their downloads. A link that opens in the browser is found in a second.
f6d9364e: Can I send the entry code right after booking?
cd91e1d9: Better not. Send the door or key box code only a day or two before arrival, once the booking is definitely confirmed and paid. That reduces the risk of the code circulating long before the stay.
02d2d067: What if the guest doesn't read the instructions?
220b175b: It happens. That's why you send a short reminder on the day of arrival with a link to the instructions, and put the answer to the most common question (Wi-Fi, entrance) at the very top of the message.
6d8faa14: How long should the message with instructions be?
59f275a3: Long enough for guests to see everything important on their phone without much scrolling. The six blocks from the template are enough. Put appliance details and city recommendations in a separate guide.
